title: DO I = 1, N — when N < 1 the loop body NEVER executes (F77 zero-trip semantic)
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE SAFE_SUM(A, N, S)
C     F77 (and F90 + modern Fortran) say: when the computed trip
C     count is <= 0, the DO body does NOT execute even once. F66
C     (pre-F77) executed the body at least once before checking.
C     Old code translated from F66 idioms may rely on the
C     once-around behaviour; modern Java for-loops match F77
C     (zero-trip).
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER N, I
      REAL    A(*), S
      S = 0.0
      DO I = 1, N
         S = S + A(I)
      END DO
      END
notes: Important on inputs where N comes from data: the legacy code may guard against N <= 0 elsewhere, or it may NOT and rely on zero-trip to return the initialised default (0.0 here). The spec must capture the zero-trip semantic AND surface whether N <= 0 is a valid input.
